messages:
Emma - AcmeCorp: hi team, hitting a wall — our production jobs started getting 429s around 10:12 UTC. happens every minute in a sawtooth pattern, ~30s of normal then spike of 429s for ~10s. no code change on our side.
Aisha - Support: thanks Emma — can you paste a sample request id / headers and the approximate qps/rpm you’re seeing? also which org key?
Emma - AcmeCorp: tenant: acme-prod, sample x-request-id: rq_01Hq9Abc, headers:

    x-request-id: rq_01Hq9Abc
    x-redwood-region: us-west-2
    x-client-retries: 2

we're doing ~1.5k requests/minute aggregated across 12 workers (mostly small prompt requests, ~60 tokens). spikes align on the minute boundary.
Aisha - Support: ok. that pattern smells like minute-window alignment (RPM buckets) — maybe a token-bucket refill clash. can you check client side whether all workers sync to a cron/heartbeat?
Emma - AcmeCorp: oh yep one of our cron syncs fires at top of minute to refresh sessions, that's likely.
Raj - Oncall: pulling metrics now. I see per-tenant RPM cap for acme-prod at 1800 rpm. traffic is spiky with bursts hitting 2100rpm at :00 each minute. upstream per-second smoothing looks disabled.
Lucas - Infra: confirmed — the tenant is hitting account-level RPM limit, server returns 429 and X-RateLimit info shows: 

    x-ratelimit-rpm: 1800
    x-ratelimit-remaining: 0
    x-ratelimit-reset: 12

Ratebot: automated alert — tenant acme-prod exceeded RPM by 17% for 6 consecutive minutes.
Aisha - Support: options: (1) immediate temporary quota bump (manual) while customer fixes client timing, (2) advise de-sync + jitter on client cron, (3) recommend batching or dedicated capacity for sustained bursts. Emma which do you prefer?
Emma - AcmeCorp: need short-term unblocking asap. can we get a temporary bump for next 24h while we rework cron + batching?
Raj - Oncall: I can apply a scoped bump to 3000rpm for 24h, but we should avoid arbitrarily large increases — will need an ops ticket. meanwhile apply client-side smoothing.
Aisha - Support: Emma, quick repro steps you can run locally to validate smoothing changes: replace synchronized cron with a randomized start (0-59s) and add exponential backoff on 429s with full jitter. small shell to simulate: 

    # loadtest: 12 workers, random jitter start
    for i in $(seq 1 12); do
      (sleep $((RANDOM%60)); while true; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"x"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate; sleep 0.8; done) &
    done

this should remove minute-alignment spikes.
Emma - AcmeCorp: thanks, will roll that now and confirm. can you kick off the temporary bump?
Aisha - Support: opened ops ticket OPS-4281 for 24h bump to 3000rpm, flagged urgency: high. Raj please approve.
Raj - Oncall: approved and applied. tenant acme-prod now 3000rpm (effective immediately). monitor for 5 minutes and post any new x-ratelimit-* headers.
Emma - AcmeCorp: saw immediate drop in 429s after bump, will push client randomization this hour and test.
Lucas - Infra: follow-up: long-term suggestions for Emma: 1) use jittered heartbeats, 2) consolidate tiny prompts into batch calls when possible, 3) enable prefix caching if prompt reuse exists, 4) consider Dedicated pool for stable high-throughput use cases.
Aisha - Support: adding checklist for customer's devs: 
- review cron alignment and add jitter (0-60s)
- implement exponential backoff with full jitter for 429s
- add client-side token bucket to smooth bursts
- if sustained traffic >2000rpm, request Dedicated or quota increase via support ticket

Emma - AcmeCorp: copying our SREs here, we'll test and report back in ~45m. thanks everyone :pray:
Aisha - Support: np — keep this thread updated, we'll close after 24h bump expires and you confirm mitigation.
RateBot: reminder scheduled — OPS-4281 will auto-revert quota change at 2024-04-02T11:12:00Z unless extended.
